comparator.academicYear: Currently published indicative pathway: year 2 through 2025–2026, year 3 through 2026–2027; later details pending
comparator.sourceNotes: The Dutch-language first year has ten compulsory 6-EC courses; from year two the three named specialisations are Accounting, Finance and Economics & Policy, taught in English. The selected Economics & Policy year-two pathway has ten compulsory 6-EC courses. The year-three International Economics and Policy pathway comprises four named 6-EC specialist courses (24 EC), genuinely free space for study abroad, internship or electives (24 EC), and a 12-EC economics thesis. The public year-two curriculum is stated to apply through 2025–2026 and the year-three curriculum through 2026–2027; later schedules are not established. This is a coherent currently published illustrative 180-EC pathway, not a promise for a Fall 2026 entrant.

These choices serve the evidenced policy and responsible-business question, not numerical variety.

comparatorRouteSelection.basis: Radboud currently identifies Accounting, Finance and Economics & Policy in year two and the corresponding International Economics and Policy specialisation in year three. This route best represents the generic bachelor’s broad economics, international markets and public policy identity; Accounting and Finance are narrower. The route was selected from the external programme before assessing UCR fit.

alternativeSelection.assessment: The closest UCR response retains economic theory, finance, business and quantitative research. The second route shifts five substantive courses toward economic policy, responsible firms and sustainability. Both remain feasible and differ by five courses each. Separate specialist finance and accounting routes are evidenced but cannot form credible distinct 24-course programmes from the current UCR offer without weak substitutes.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: Matched explicitly after semantic review: Inleiding tot Economie en de economie corresponds to Introduction to Economics.
Matched explicitly after semantic review: Macro-economie corresponds to International Macroeconomics.
Matched explicitly after semantic review: Micro-economie corresponds to Microeconomics & Behavior.
Matched explicitly after semantic review: Behavioural and Experimental Economics corresponds to Behavioral Economics.
Matched explicitly after semantic review: Public Economics and Finance corresponds to Public Economics.
No included UCR course directly treats development economics as an economic subfield.
Sociology and public economics touch inequality but do not directly teach labour economics.
General market strategy and behavioural economics do not replace a dedicated game-theory course.
Modern history and business study do not directly teach the disciplinary history of economic thought.
Matched explicitly after semantic review: Data Analyse & Statistiek corresponds to Research Methods & Statistics.
Matched explicitly after semantic review: Wiskunde voor Economie en Bedrijfseconomie corresponds to Mathematical Methods.
Matched explicitly after semantic review: Applied Methods in Economic and Policy corresponds to Introduction to Data Science.
Matched explicitly after semantic review: Toegepaste Econometrie 1 corresponds to Econometrics.
UCR has one econometrics course aligned to the first applied sequence; no separately credited second stage appears.
Matched explicitly after semantic review: Inleiding tot Bedrijfseconomie en Financiële Economie corresponds to Entrepreneurship & Business Foundations.
Matched explicitly after semantic review: Accounting & Control (NL) corresponds to Accounting & Corporate Finance.
Matched explicitly after semantic review: Corporate Finance corresponds to Money, Banking & Finance.
Matched explicitly after semantic review: Inleiding Marketing en Strategie corresponds to Marketing & Consumer Engagement.
Matched explicitly after semantic review: Markets and Strategy corresponds to Strategy & Digital Transformation.
The UCR banking/finance course does not separately reproduce international financial policy.
UCR studies environmental governance and impacts, but no scheduled course directly teaches the economics of sustainability at Radboud’s scope.
The UCR macroeconomics course already aligns to Radboud macroeconomics; global business is not a direct substitute for international economic theory.
No single scheduled course covers the advanced topical seminar in international economics and policy as such.
Matched explicitly after semantic review: Academische en Professionele Vaardigheden corresponds to Personal & Professional Development.
Radboud allows 24 EC of genuine free-choice space for study abroad, internship or electives; UCR courses have their own separately represented curriculum.
Radboud requires a twelve-credit economics thesis; UCR independent research appears only as a comparison-only option.

notes.text: Radboud provides a dedicated multi-year economics and business economics curriculum with a named specialisation, staged econometrics and a required economics thesis. UCR combines economics, business, quantitative research, policy and sustainability but does not reproduce that disciplinary depth or mandatory thesis. Radboud also permits 24 EC of free choice in year three.
